sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling followed by the prespecified measurable finite code \(Z=\kappa(O)\), fixed before sampling.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from one unknown \(M_0\in M_G\).
sampling_model.treatment: Interventions enter only through the fixed graph-native query \(Q\); treatment assignment need not be randomized.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is imposed because the target is a restricted identified set rather than an inverse-propensity functional.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The sampled nuisance is the fixed-code law \(p_0\), covered by exact multinomial inversion. The full-class theorem concerns only the identified set induced by that code and optimizes over \(M_G\); executable certificates separately require rational \(\alpha\) and restrict structural inputs to \(M_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

body.tldr: For a known acyclic ADMG with compact mixed variables and a fixed measurable finite observational code, an abstract district-coupled response sieve yields a two-sided exact-coded-law lifting and exact finite-sample coverage of the full Lipschitz-class identified set induced by that code, not by the unbinned law. The construction is informed by Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim's finite exact canonicalization and Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis's mixed-variable graphwise Wasserstein approximation, but asserts no containment between their classes and this one; neither comparator provides the joint two-sided exact-coded-law, uniform query-error, and whole-set finite-sample guarantee. Computation is a separate theorem for rational support boxes, rational \(\alpha\), semialgebraic code cells, and a specified rational piecewise-polynomial or ReLU grammar with checker-certified integrals. Certified near-extremal neural witnesses form an inner interval, while Autobounds and the UA-DCM Parents' Labor Supply analysis are implementation and decision consumers rather than sources of additional headline claims.

project_justification.gap: Definition 2.3 and Theorem 2.4 of Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim establish finite exact canonicalization. Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis define a finite-sample estimator and establish mixed-variable graphwise Wasserstein approximation together with almost-sure asymptotic consistency and bracketing. Neither comparator supplies two-sided preservation of a fixed finite coded observational law with uniform query error and exact finite-sample coverage of the entire coded-law identified set, and no inclusion between their model classes and \(M_G\) is claimed. Existing global-optimization work does not state the rational likelihood-region, coded-law, and integral encoding needed for independent certificates.
project_justification.niche: The mathematical validity problem and the computational certification problem require different scopes. The full Lipschitz class supports a noncomputational theorem for the identified set induced by a fixed measurable finite code; a rationally encoded subclass supports a finite program with explicit likelihood, coded-law, and integral constraints, target extrema, and reproducible certificates.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the full-class two-sided lifting and exact whole-set coverage for the fixed coded law, then proves finite termination and soundness only for rational boxes, rational \(\alpha\), semialgebraic code cells, rational piecewise-polynomial or ReLU mechanisms and queries, and exact or certified outer integral encodings. Near-extremal neural witnesses are checked against explicit neural extrema, and their formal residual is separated from mesh, integral-enclosure, and optimization errors. Autobounds supplies an implementation setting; the UA-DCM Parents' Labor Supply sign check is recorded only as a downstream consequence of outer-set containment.

body.related_work: Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim's Definition 2.3 introduces canonical SCMs, and their Theorem 2.4 establishes sufficiency for finite-domain counterfactual distributions. Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis define their neural bound estimator at finite sample, establish mixed-variable graphwise approximation in Wasserstein distance, and prove almost-sure asymptotic consistency and bracketing. These are two distinct inputs to the construction, but neither supplies two-sided preservation of a prespecified finite coded observational law together with a uniform query-error bound and exact finite-sample coverage of the whole coded-law identified set. The proposal asserts no containment or extension relation between either comparator's class and \(M_G\). Choe et al. quotient finite canonical domains and inform the discrete side of the construction. Duarte et al. provide anytime numerical outer bounds and solver-reported epsilon sharpness for discrete causal polynomial programs; the computable theorem tightens the trust boundary only on the declared rational grammar by producing independently checkable rational certificates for the explicit multinomial, coded-law, and integral encoding. Chafai and Concordet provide likelihood-level exact multinomial inversion, while Romano and Shaikh supply the whole-identified-set coverage criterion under asymptotic calibration. Xia et al., Balazadeh et al., and Tan et al. motivate graph-compatible neural witnesses, but do not certify exact coded-law feasibility together with explicit near-extremality. Cheung, Gleixner, and Steffy, Cook et al., Bunel et al., and Shi et al. inform the certificate calculus. Rahman et al. supply the UA-DCM formulation and Parents' Labor Supply application; here that application is only a consumer of certified outer-set containment, and no new numerical result is asserted for it.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact finite-sample coverage concerns the identified set induced by the prespecified measurable finite code \(\kappa\), not the identified set under the entire unbinned continuous observational law. The interval \(I_{\mathrm{abs}}\) is valid over the full Lipschitz class but need not be computable. The executable interval \(I_{\mathrm{out}}\) covers only the explicitly declared rationally certifiable subclass, and certified outer integral enclosures are charged to the total optimization tolerance. No inclusion or limiting relation is asserted between the separate atomic bow diagnostic and the bounded-density continuous-noise class. Fixed-tolerance certificate termination does not imply polynomial runtime.
body.honest_scope: The exact multinomial inversion is settled once deterministic outer lifting is available. The central theorem target is the two-sided exact-coded-law response lifting over the full Lipschitz class and its linear endpoint error, always relative to the fixed measurable code. Rational branch-and-bound soundness and finite termination are claimed only for rational compact boxes, rational \(\alpha\), semialgebraic coding cells, the specified rational piecewise-polynomial or ReLU grammar, and exact or convergent checker-certified integral enclosures. The binary bow result is a separate discrete atomic-response sanity proposition. Vanishing neural representation residual \(\Gamma_n\) remains open; every reported neural witness must nevertheless carry an independently checked feasibility and near-extremality tolerance.
